text.p: Eurotunnel Executive Chairman Patrick Ponsolle on Tuesday expressed satisfaction with the decision of the French and British governments to extend conditionally the Channel Tunnel operator's licence.
"I am extremely pleased for our shareholders about today's statement of the British and French governments relating to the extension of our concession," Ponsolle said in a statement.
Britain and France said earlier on Tuesday they were ready to extend Eurotunnel's licence to at least 99 years from 65 years.
In return, the company will pay the two governments a total of around 25 percent of its net profit after the year 2052.
Eurotunnel needed to get the licence extension to win shareholders' backing for a plan to restructure its 70 billion francs ($11.9 billion) of bank debt. Shareholders vote on the plan on July 10.

"It is quite legitimate, in my opinion, that an extension of the concession up to at least 99 years in total allows our shareholders to have a reasonable hope of a satisfactory return on their initial investment," Ponsolle said.
"I would have liked to reach a complete and definitive agreement but the statement of the two governments represents a decisive step towards such an agreement." $ = 5.883 French Francs)
